title: Vice-President inaugurates fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam in Varanasi
subtitle:
Kashi and Tamil Nadu share a civilisational bond spanning thousands of years: Vice-President
Kashi Tamil Sangamam is not merely a cultural event but a movement to strengthen national unity: Vice-President
Vice-President releases Thirukkural translations in 50 languages, including 10 foreign languages
Vice-President Calls upon people to take pride in their mother tongue while respecting all languages
Vice-President Envisions a future in which the waters of the Ganga reach the Cauvery through the national river-linking initiative
body_text:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS 5.0) in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. On the occasion, he released editions of the Thirukkural translated into 50 languages, including 10 foreign languages. Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS 5.0) at Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, today, in the presence of Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, and other distinguished dignitaries.

Inspired by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the centuries-old civilisational, cultural and linguistic bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, while strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.

This year’s theme, “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen” (Let Us Learn the Thirukkural), seeks to take the timeless wisdom and universal values of Thiruvalluvar's Thirukkural to students and youth across the country. — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 28, 2026 Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that Kashi and Tamil Nadu share a deep-rooted civilisational, cultural and spiritual relationship that goes back thousands of years. Describing Kashi as the spiritual capital of the world, he said that the city holds a special place in the hearts of Tamil people, for whom a visit to Kashi and the darshan of Baba Vishwanath is a cherished spiritual aspiration. Addressing the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam in Varanasi, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the timeless civilisational bonds between Kashi and Tamil Nadu and the importance of celebrating India’s linguistic and cultural diversity.

During the occasion, he released the Thirukkural in 50 languages, including 10 foreign languages, at the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam in Varanasi.

This landmark initiative takes the timeless wisdom of Saint Thiruvalluvar to a wider global audience, celebrating the universal values enshrined in this great Tamil classic.! — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 28, 2026 The Vice-President observed that despite India’s immense linguistic, regional and cultural diversity, a shared civilisational and spiritual ethos has always united the country. He noted that this enduring bond inspired the launch of Kashi Tamil Sangamam under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He further stated that the initiative has evolved beyond a cultural programme into a significant national movement that rekindles the historic ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi and strengthens the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat. This year’s edition is centred on the theme “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”, with the objective of taking the timeless wisdom and ethical values of the Thirukkural, particularly to students and young people. The Vice-President described the Thirukkural as a universal guide to life, whose message of equality, humanism and righteousness transcends the boundaries of language, region and nation. He urged people to study its teachings and put them into practice in their daily lives. He noted that the translation of the Thirukkural into 50 languages, including foreign languages, was a significant achievement for Tamil language and literature and a tribute to the universal relevance of Thiruvalluvar’s teachings. Recalling that the first edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam saw the Thirukkural published in 13 languages, followed by translations into 16 additional languages in the second edition, he said that its availability in 50 languages in the fifth edition marks an important milestone in taking Tamil literary heritage to a wider audience. Emphasising the importance of linguistic harmony, the Vice-President said that everyone should take pride in their mother tongue while respecting the languages of others. He said "Love for one’s own language should never become hostility towards another language". He said that India’s strength lies in its many languages and shared ideals. He also recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s reference to the Sangam-era poet Kaniyan Pungundranar’s celebrated words, “Yaadhum Oore, Yaavarum Kelir”, at the United Nations, bringing the Tamil ideal of universal brotherhood to the global stage. The Vice-President called upon the youth to draw inspiration from leaders such as Perunthalaivar K. Kamaraj and Pasumpon Muthuramalinga Thevar and to uphold the spirit of national unity. He said that the younger generation has an important role in carrying forward India’s civilisational values and strengthening the bonds that unite the country. Referring to Uttar Pradesh’s development under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, the Vice-President appreciated the transformation of the State and its progress in areas including economic development and public safety. He also recalled his long-standing association and friendship with the Chief Minister, which dates back to their time together in Parliament in 1998. Speaking about India’s aspirations for 2047, the Vice-President said that the goal of Viksit Bharat must extend beyond economic growth. He said that India should also emerge as a global example of civilisational heritage, cultural values and humanism. He highlighted the relevance of India’s traditional philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah in a world facing conflict, uncertainty and divisions. Concluding his address, the Vice-President expressed confidence in the vision of connecting the country’s rivers, stating that a day would come when the waters of the Ganga would reach the Cauvery. Around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, representing diverse sections of society, including students, teachers, writers, journalists, farmers, artisans, women,and industry representatives , are participating in this edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam. The programme is being organised through the coordinated efforts of the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education; IIT Madras; Banaras Hindu University; the Central Institute of Classical Tamil, Chennai; the Government of Uttar Pradesh; and various Ministries and departments of the Government of India. The Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath; Union Minister of Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi; Uttar Pradesh Ministers Shri Anil Rajbhar, Shri Ravindra Jaiswal, Shri Dayashankar Mishra and Shri Hansraj Vishwakarma; Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Smt. Deepti Umashankar; Chairman of the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti, Shri Chamu Krishna Shastry; Director of IIT Madras, Shri V. Kamakoti; Vice-Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University, Prof. Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi; spiritual leaders, scholars, delegates from Tamil Nadu, students and members of the public attended the event. Earlier, the Vice-President, accompanied by the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, visited Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Shri Kaal Bhairav Temple in Varanasi and offered prayers.
